anomalies.observed: The main-pump MOSFET T6 (IRLR2905) gate net /NET0089 contains only the 100 Ω drive resistor R21 from ESP32 IO10 and the 10 kΩ pull-up R16; it has no BT3904 collector connected to it. The second BT3904, T7, whose base is driven from the FLOAT_LOW signal IO0 through R48, has its collector tied to /NET0059, the ATO-valve gate net, together with T2 and T8.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that the main circulation pump MOSFET is gate-driven through a 100 Ω resistor and pre-driven by a BT3904 NPN level shifter, and that float switches provide low-level pump cutoff interlocks. The low-level float path should therefore be connected to the main-pump gate net (/NET0089) through a BT3904 collector, not to the ATO-valve gate net.

evidence.quote: T2 — IRLR2905 ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter).
float-switch interlocks for low-level pump cutoff and high-level overflow protection

anomalies.impact: The intended hardware low-level pump cutoff interlock is missing: the main pump can remain enabled by GPIO10 even when the low-level float condition is asserted, while the low-level float instead disables the ATO valve. This can allow dry-running of the circulation pump and changes the intended safety interlock behavior.

parsed.summary: The connectivity shows the main pump gate net lacks the BT3904 predriver/interlock described in the specification; the low-level float transistor T7 is tied to the ATO-valve gate net instead of the pump gate net, which is a deviation from the intended float-switch pump-cutoff interlock.
